scenarios.name: Prolonged Inflationary Pressures and Further Rate Hikes
scenarios.description: Persistent high inflation continues to push the Federal Reserve to maintain elevated interest rates, leading to slower economic growth and potential recession risks.

impacts.explanation: Sustained high inflation erodes purchasing power and prompts central bank to keep rates elevated, reducing consumer spending and business investment.
Continued rate hikes to combat inflation push short-term policy rates higher.
Higher inflation expectations and risk premium increase long-term bond yields.
Elevated interest rates dampen investment and consumption, slowing economic expansion.

scenarios.reasoning: Based on historical pattern where persistent inflation leads to sustained rate hikes, which historically correlate with reduced real GDP growth. Base rates suggest continued tightening pressure.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems

scenarios.name: Geopolitical Escalation (Russia-Ukraine/Middle East Conflicts)
scenarios.description: Escalating regional conflicts disrupt global supply chains, drive energy price spikes, and increase import costs, putting downward pressure on the U.S. economy.

impacts.explanation: Increased demand for imported energy and goods due to conflict-driven supply disruptions worsens the trade deficit.
Energy price shocks from geopolitical instability feed into broader CPI inflation.
Disruptions can lead to job losses in export-oriented sectors and manufacturing.

scenarios.reasoning: Historical precedent shows that major conflicts trigger commodity price spikes and trade imbalances. Base rates indicate heightened uncertainty.

scenarios.name: Supply Chain Disruption and Trade War Intensification
scenarios.description: Ongoing trade tensions and pandemic-related supply chain bottlenecks reduce industrial production and retail sales growth.

impacts.explanation: Disrupted inputs and logistics slow manufacturing output.
Supply shortages and higher input costs reduce consumer spending.
Import surges to replace disrupted supplies worsen the trade deficit.

scenarios.reasoning: Trade frictions directly affect production capacity and consumer confidence. Historical data supports this correlation.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between inside and outside views

scenarios.name: Fiscal Stimulus and Infrastructure Spending
scenarios.description: Government spending on infrastructure projects stimulates demand, boosting employment and economic activity.

impacts.explanation: Direct government spending creates jobs and increases aggregate demand.
Job creation from public works lowers unemployment.
Increased borrowing raises the national debt burden.

scenarios.reasoning: Fiscal stimulus typically boosts GDP and employment in the short term, though it carries long-term debt implications. Base rates show moderate stimulus levels.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work

scenarios.name: Currency Devaluation and Capital Flight
scenarios.description: Weak dollar and capital outflows reduce foreign investment inflows and put upward pressure on the currency.

impacts.explanation: Stronger dollar makes borrowing more expensive domestically, supporting rates.
Capital flight increases demand for Treasuries, pushing yields up.
Debt level remains largely unchanged in the short term despite currency shifts.

scenarios.reasoning: A weaker dollar attracts speculative capital but also increases import costs, creating complex feedback loops. Historical precedents support this dynamic.

methodology: Applied Tetlock's superforecasting methodology: probabilistic thinking with explicit probability assignments, continuous updating of beliefs, balancing inside/outside views, and granular decomposition of economic systems into measurable components.
geopoliticalSummary: Global tensions persist with ongoing conflicts in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. US-China strategic competition remains high, and energy security concerns drive protectionist policies. These factors create volatility in trade and commodity markets.
geoeconomicSummary: US trade deficits widen due to increased import dependence on adversarial nations. Supply chain resilience efforts face challenges from geopolitical fragmentation. Currency dynamics reflect divergent monetary policies across major economies.
currentEventsSummary: Recent developments include elevated inflation persisting above target, continued Federal Reserve rate hikes, expanding trade deficit, and ongoing geopolitical conflicts affecting energy and commodity markets. Nonfarm payrolls have remained stable while housing starts decline.
